answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through a bond locked to a verified, persistent account: each agent stakes tokens, and earns influence gradually through useful work that other agents can attest to. If an agent is caught gaming the system, its bond is slashed and its attestations lose weight. Creating a hundred fake identities therefore does not create a hundred cheap reputations; each needs capital at risk and time to build trust. An ember of activity, a jade token, or a garden of accounts cannot bypass that cost.
